pages.text: A mob will become bound when in a $(bold)block focus$() that is influenced by certain items. These items are different for each mob, and tend to be antithetical to their nature. Each item contributes some amount of influence to the binding, and the total influence must be at least thrice the mob's maximum health to bind it. A bound mob will be unable to move or attack.

Many mobs have an associated spirit type. They can be bound by its opposite.$(br2)For instance, creepers are phlogiston-aligned and require 60 binding influence, so they can be bound by hallows containing at least 60 total water spirits. Some mobs have additional spirit types that can bind or heal them.$(br2)Spirits are often the most compact form of binding, but require extra preparation.
A creeper bound by three hallowed prismarine crystals, each with 20 water spirits.

Mobs can leave their binding focus while remaining bound, but only if the chalk of the diagram is not tampered with at all.$(br2)If the diagram ever changes such that there is no longer enough valid influence, the binding will break. Mobs that break their binding become either hostile or panicked towards the closest player, and receive a brief power-up.

Minor mobs will stay bound indefinitely. But mobs with more than 20 max health that can attack (or any mob with more than 100 max health) will slowly attack their binding, draining spirits/health or destroying items. The rate of this increases exponentially with the mob's max health. They will always target the most $(italic)unique$() influence; e.g. if a hoglin is bound by seven warped fungi and a chain, it will attack the chain.

If a mob attempts to drain a binding and the binding is not in a loaded chunk, it will break the binding. Fortunately, the $(l:otherverse:items/biome_brazier)biome brazier$() allows a Practitioner to keep chunks loaded.$(br2)Tamed mobs only require 1 influence to become bound.

You can see the effect each item has on a mob in JEI/EMI by clicking its idol or spawn egg. The numbers next to the black chain icons indicates the influence each item/spirit provides, and the total influence necessary to bind the mob. Note that some mobs can be bound by other bound mobs; e.g. creepers can be bound by bound cats, and a warden can bind any mob capable of attacking its binding.

For mobs that attack their bindings, a crossed chain icon indicates how often and severely they do so. "4/164s" means that every 164 seconds, it will destroy one item, drain 4 spirits from a hallow, or do 4 damage to a mob that's helping bind it.$(br2)You can right-click a bound mob with an empty hand to switch between simple behaviors. But for more complex routines, you'll need a contract.
